summary.text:
We need answer only valid JSON with specified keys. Need produce concise architecture plan <=2000 words. Must not enumerate exhaustive traces. Need include state_machine list states/transitions, timer_plan, priorities, initial_values, scan_execution_order explicit 4-stage, formal_assertions optional list with id formula over declared input/output port names.

We need design PLC architecture for automated production line. Need be careful semantics: inputs sampled, outputs after scan. States likely WAIT_A, MOVE_AB, WAIT_B, MOVE_BC, WAIT_C, DONE? Initial phase WAIT_A. Mode manual/auto. Requirement: automatic mode: when product arrives at A, SensorA detects, after operator triggers ButtonA, motor forward to move product to B. When arrives at B SensorB detects, motor stops, after ButtonB motor forward to C. When arrives at C SensorC detects, motor stops, after ButtonC CompletionLight on. When product taken away SensorC no longer detects, light off. Need maybe automatic phase DONE after ButtonC? The atomic props include done_phase post-phase DONE, wait_phase WAIT_A/B/C, move_phase MOVE_AB/BC. Initial phase WAIT_A. They mention P7: in auto, WAIT_A/B/C keeps all outputs off, MOVE_AB/BC drives MotorForward only, DONE lights CompletionLight only. So state machine should have DONE state with light on. Transition: WAIT_C + SensorC + ButtonC -> DONE (light on). DONE + !SensorC -> WAIT_A? Also "When product is taken away ... light off." likely DONE when SensorC true, light on. When removed, go WAIT_A. If in DONE and SensorC still true, keep DONE. Need handle arrival transitions: WAIT_A? Actually when product arrives at A, SensorA detects, after ButtonA, motor starts forward to B. State WAIT_A waiting for product at A and ButtonA. At WAIT_A, if SensorA & ButtonA -> MOVE_AB? But P4 arrival formula uses pre-phase MOVE_AB and SensorB OR pre-phase MOVE_BC and SensorC -> !fwd. So arrival at destination stops movement. Therefore MOVE_AB transitions to WAIT_B when SensorB. In MOVE_AB, fwd true until arrival SensorB, then stop and go WAIT_B. But if same scan sensor arrives, output !fwd per P4. Need transition affects same observed scan: if MOVE_AB and SensorB, next phase WAIT_B and output fwd false in same scan. Good.

MOVE_BC transitions to WAIT_C on SensorC. WAIT_C: after ButtonC and SensorC -> DONE, light on. What if sensor C removed? In WAIT_C if product leaves? Probably assumption only one product, sensor not contradictory; if removed maybe remain WAIT_C? Could go WAIT_A? Requirement only DONE removal. The phase sequence should perhaps WAIT_C + SensorC + ButtonC -> DONE; DONE + !SensorC -> WAIT_A. If DONE and SensorC false, light off. If mode manual, clear auto state and completion; return to automatic waits for A. Need mode handling: "Entering manual mode clears automatic state and completion; return to automatic waits for A." So when Mode false, phase = WAIT_A? Or manual state? Need state machine include MANUAL? We can model phase remains WAIT_A when manual, outputs manual. But P7 only auto. In manual mode, auto phase cleared to WAIT_A and completion off. Transition: Mode=0 -> reset auto phase WAIT_A, light off. Mode=1 -> WAIT_A. Need ensure entering manual clears state. Could have states manual? But atomic phase only WAIT_A etc. For state_machine, can include operational auto states plus MANUAL? However initial phase WAIT_A per initial. In manual, maybe state MANUAL? But P7 auto only. initial_conditions phase WAIT_A. Could include mode as separate variable. But state_machine list can say states WAIT_A... DONE, MANUAL_RESET? Need not overcomplicate. Need clean PLC design.

Need timer_plan: timers required, PT durations, reset conditions. Are any timers required? Specification doesn't mention delays/timers. Could have no timers. But key requires timer_plan. Could state empty list? Need maybe include "none" or []? It says timer_plan: timers required, PT durations, reset conditions. We can include [] if no timers required. But maybe need timer for button debouncing? Not specified. Avoid adding behavior. Could include no timers. But maybe they expect timer plan with no timers. We can provide {"timers":[],"notes":"..."}? But key should likely be list. The prompt says timer_plan: timers required, PT durations, reset conditions. Could be list of objects. Use [] and maybe explanation? To satisfy, include list with object "none"? Better valid JSON: "timer_plan": [] . But then no reset conditions. Could include "timer_plan": [{"name":"No timers required", ...}]? That might be weird. Maybe include empty array is acceptable. We can add a note? But keys only. We can include "timer_plan": {"timers": [], "note": "No timers required; transitions are level/edge-free per assumptions."} Is that okay? It asks "timer_plan: timers required, PT durations, reset conditions" not necessarily list. Use object with timers array. But "Return complete JSON with keys: - state_machine: list... - timer_plan: timers required..." Could be any. I'll use "timer_plan": [] with maybe no timers. But formal_assertions optional. Need include formal assertions maybe with G formulas using port names. Must use declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. Can include formulas from LTL. Need ensure syntax uses port names. E.g. "G(!(MotorForward && MotorReverse))". For manual: "G((!Mode) -> ((MotorForward <-> (ForwardButton && !ReverseButton)) && (MotorReverse <-> (ReverseButton && !ForwardButton))))". For auto direction: "G(Mode -> !MotorReverse)". Arrival: Need express pre-phase? Formal assertions over port names only? They said over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. Could include mode and sensor. For arrival: "G((Mode && SensorB) -> ?)" Not exactly because only when moving AB. But if SensorB true while auto maybe motor should stop? Requirement: when arrives at B, motor stops. But if in WAIT_B, fwd already off. Could assert "G(Mode && SensorB -> !MotorForward)"? But what about moving from B to C with SensorB still true? Assumption sensors non-contradictory, maybe product leaves SensorB. But could be okay? Actually if SensorB true, motor should be stopped? In WAIT_B, yes. But after ButtonB, motor starts forward to move from B to C; SensorB may still detect until product moves off. If we assert G(Mode && SensorB -> !MotorForward), it would prevent starting movement from B while SensorB still true. Requirement: "When product arrives at B, SensorB detects, motor stops, and after operator triggers complete via ButtonB, motor starts forward to C." If SensorB remains true at button press, then motor should start despite SensorB true? Maybe product at B, sensor detects; after processing complete, motor moves product away, so SensorB may still be true initially. Thus P4 formula uses pre-phase MOVE_AB and SensorB to stop, not any SensorB. So formal assertion using port names only cannot express phase. Could include internal variables? They said over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. So maybe avoid phase-dependent formulas. Include only universal safety: interlock, manual behavior, auto no reverse, completion light when finish? Finish requires phase. Could use ButtonC & SensorC & Mode -> CompletionLight? But if in WAIT_C, yes; if already DONE, light true. If in MOVE_BC and SensorC true but not ButtonC? no. If in WAIT_C and ButtonC true, light. Could assert "G((Mode && SensorC && ButtonC) -> CompletionLight)" but this may not hold if in DONE? It holds. If in WAIT_A with SensorC and ButtonC? Assumption only one product, but could hold? If product at C, phase likely WAIT_C or DONE. But formal over ports only might be okay. Removal: "G((Mode && !SensorC) -> !CompletionLight)"? Is this true? In auto WAIT/ MOVE, light off. In DONE, if !SensorC transition to WAIT_A and light off same scan. So yes, in auto, !SensorC -> !CompletionLight. But in manual, also light off. Could assert "G(!SensorC -> !CompletionLight)"? What if manual? light off. Yes. But what if CompletionLight on and SensorC false? Requirement says off. So universal: G(!SensorC -> !CompletionLight). But if SensorC true and ButtonC not pressed, light off. Could assert "G(CompletionLight -> SensorC)" (light only when product at C). That's an invariant. But maybe completion light could be manually set? No. So include.

Need include scan_execution_order explicit 4-stage exactly as required. Need describe stage 1 edge sampling; stage 2 safety/reset priority & state transitions; stage 3 unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF; stage 4 unified output assignments. Need be explicit. Since no timers, stage 3 still state "call no timer FBs; placeholders unconditional if present". Need mention edge sampling for buttons? Buttons are level signals accepted only in corresponding station wait, one phase transition per call. Edge sampling may be for buttons? In auto, "after operator triggers processing complete signal via ButtonA" - could be level signal accepted when in wait. Assumptions: "Buttons are level signals accepted only in their corresponding station wait. One phase transition accepted per call." So no edge required. But scan order stage 1 edge sampling: sample inputs, compute rising edges for manual buttons? But manual is level. We can say capture raw inputs and optional rising edges for buttons, but logic uses level for manual and station acceptance. Need stage 1 "edge sampling" explicit. Maybe define rising-edge flags for ButtonA/B/C? But assumptions say level signals accepted only in corresponding station wait. If we use rising edge, would differ. Better: stage 1 sample inputs and compute edge flags only for diagnostics or not used? The required scan order says "1. edge sampling". We need say sample all inputs; derive button edge flags if needed but station buttons are consumed as level-qualified by phase, not edge-gated. Or "edge sampling: latch current inputs and compute R_TRIG edges for buttons; however auto station buttons are level-accepted per assumptions, so edge flags are not used for phase transitions." That satisfies.

Need state_machine list of states and transitions. Need include mode transitions? Could define states WAIT_A, MOVE_AB, WAIT_B, MOVE_BC, WAIT_C, DONE. Maybe also MANUAL? But if Mode false, phase forced WAIT_A. Could include "MANUAL" state? Initial phase WAIT_A. But mode switch changes behavior. The state machine can have superstate AUTO and MANUAL. However phase variable only auto. To be concise, use states:
- WAIT_A: auto idle at A; outputs off; waiting SensorA & ButtonA.
- MOVE_AB: forward to B; outputs MF; transition to WAIT_B on SensorB (same scan output off per arrival).
- WAIT_B: at B; outputs off; wait SensorB & ButtonB -> MOVE_BC. Actually if SensorB is true from arrival, ButtonB triggers. If product not at B? Wait for SensorB & ButtonB. Since arrival set WAIT_B when SensorB true, ButtonB may be pressed later. Need if SensorB false? Maybe remain. Transition on ButtonB & SensorB. 
- MOVE_BC: forward to C; transition to WAIT_C on SensorC.
- WAIT_C: at C; outputs off; wait SensorC & ButtonC -> DONE.
- DONE: light on while SensorC; transition to WAIT_A on !SensorC.
Mode false: any state -> WAIT_A, clear light. Mode true from manual -> WAIT_A. Need "Entering manual mode clears automatic state and completion; return to automatic waits for A." So on Mode falling edge? Or level? If Mode false, force WAIT_A and light off. When Mode true, phase already WAIT_A. If Mode switches false while in MOVE, motor stops. Need output manual logic: In manual mode, MotorForward = ForwardButton && !ReverseButton; MotorReverse = ReverseButton && !ForwardButton; CompletionLight false. Auto outputs from phase. Need interlock. If Mode false, auto phase reset. In scan, stage 2 safety/reset priority: mode change to manual overrides, force phase WAIT_A, clear completion. Also safety interlock: never both outputs; if both requests, both off (manual conflict) or auto prevents reverse. Need priority: manual mode overrides auto? Mode false manual. In manual, forward/reverse interlock. In auto, forward only. Arrival stop priority. Completion removal priority.

Need initial_values: include inputs? initial values for variables. Need include outputs false, phase WAIT_A, maybe edge flags false, mode current? Inputs maybe not initialized. Provide variables: MotorForward=false, MotorReverse=false, CompletionLight=false, phase="WAIT_A", prevForwardButton=false, prevReverseButton=false, prevButtonA/B/C=false, maybe modePrev=false? Need if initial Mode? Not specified. Use declared initial conditions. Could include "ModePrev": false? But if Mode initially true? Not relevant. Initial values for internal variables. Need include "autoPhase": "WAIT_A" or "phase". The prompt initial_conditions uses "phase": "WAIT_A". Use "phase": "WAIT_A". Also include "MotorForward": false etc. Maybe "manualModeLatched": false. But keep concise.

Need formal_assertions optional list. Need maybe include 6 assertions. Must use G(...) syntax. Need ensure formulas over port names. We can include:
A1 Interlock: "G(!(MotorForward && MotorReverse))"
A2 Manual mapping: "G((!Mode) -> ((MotorForward <-> (ForwardButton && !ReverseButton)) && (MotorReverse <-> (ReverseButton && !ForwardButton))))"
A3 Auto no reverse: "G(Mode -> !MotorReverse)"
A4 Completion implies product at C: "G(CompletionLight -> SensorC)" maybe holds if DONE with SensorC true. What if light on due to finish and sensor C true. Removal off. Good. But if manual? light false. Good.
A5 No light if C absent: "G(!SensorC -> !CompletionLight)" (same as A4 contrapositive? A4 G(light -> SensorC) equivalent to G(!SensorC -> !light). So redundant. Could use "G((Mode && SensorC && ButtonC) -> CompletionLight)" but may be too strong? If auto and sensor C true and ButtonC true in WAIT_C, light true. If already DONE, true. If in other auto phase with sensor C true? Assumption one product, could not. If manual, Mode false. So okay. But ButtonC may be true while in WAIT_A? Mode auto and sensor C true? impossible if one product at A? Could be contradictory? Assumption only one product; but if product at C, phase should be WAIT_C/DONE. Could assert. But formal over ports only, maybe safe. 
A6 Auto forward only in move? Need phase not accessible. Could assert "G(Mode && (SensorA || SensorB) && !SensorC -> !MotorReverse)"? Not necessary.
Maybe include "G(Mode && SensorB -> !MotorForward)"? As discussed, could be false during MOVE_BC if SensorB still true. But assumption sensor detects product arrived; after ButtonB, product leaves, but same scan? If SensorB still true when ButtonB pressed, MOVE_BC and fwd true while SensorB true. So don't include.
Need maybe assert "G(Mode && SensorC -> !MotorForward)"? When moving BC and SensorC arrival, P4 says stop same scan. If SensorC true while WAIT_C/DONE, fwd false. But in MOVE_BC before arrival, SensorC false. So "G(Mode && SensorC -> !MotorForward)" seems valid? At the scan when SensorC becomes true in MOVE_BC, transition to WAIT_C and output off same scan. So yes. Similarly SensorB -> !MotorForward? At scan SensorB true in MOVE_AB, stop. But after ButtonB in WAIT_B, if SensorB still true and we start MOVE_BC, output fwd true while SensorB true. That would violate. So not. SensorC has no subsequent move, so SensorC -> !MotorForward is safe. Could include "G(Mode && SensorC -> !MotorForward)" and "G(Mode && SensorC && ButtonC -> CompletionLight)". But P5 finish. Maybe include.

Need maybe include formal assertion for manual neutral conflict: "G((!Mode && ForwardButton && ReverseButton) -> (!MotorForward && !MotorReverse))". But A2 covers mapping. Good.

Need ensure JSON valid, no markdown. Need no extra text. Need complete JSON.

Let's craft state_machine as list of objects. Each state object with name, entry/do output expectations, transitions list. Need at most 2000 words. Keep concise.

State machine:
[
{"state":"WAIT_A","outputs":"all off","transitions":[{"when":"Mode==FALSE","target":"WAIT_A","action":"clear auto state and CompletionLight"},{"when":"Mode==TRUE && SensorA && ButtonA","target":"MOVE_AB","action":"start forward; one transition per scan"}]}
...
But Mode false transition from every state? To avoid repeating, can include global transition object separately? State_machine is list of states and transitions. Could include top-level "global_transitions"? But asked list of states and transitions. Use list states with transitions and a separate "global_transitions"? JSON key state_machine can be object? They said state_machine: list of states and transitions. Could be list containing states. To include global, add state "GLOBAL_MODE_RESET" with transitions. But better include a "global_transitions" in each? Maybe state_machine as object with "states" and "global_transitions". But they asked list. Hmm. "state_machine: list of states and transitions" could be list of objects each with state and transitions. For mode reset, can list in each state a transition on !Mode to WAIT_A. That is repetitive but okay. Or include a first object {"name":"GLOBAL","transitions":[{"from":"ANY","when":"Mode==FALSE","target":"WAIT_A","action":"reset auto phase, clear CompletionLight"},{"from":"ANY","when":"Mode==TRUE && phase==WAIT_A","...?"}]}. But "states and transitions" maybe acceptable. I'll make state_machine as array of state objects, each with transitions. Include !Mode in each? Could be concise with "common_reset" field? To be safe, include "common_transitions": at end? But JSON structure arbitrary. Let's do state_machine: { "states": [...], "global_transitions": [...] }? But prompt says list. I think list is safer. Use list of state objects and include a "GLOBAL_MODE_RESET" pseudo-state at start with transitions from ANY. This is still list. Example:
{
 "name": "GLOBAL_MODE_RESET",
 "transitions": [
   {"from":"ANY","when":"Mode == FALSE","target":"WAIT_A","action":"clear auto phase; CompletionLight := FALSE; stop motor requests"},
   {"from":"ANY","when":"Mode == TRUE","target":"WAIT_A","action":"manual-to-auto entry; only from WAIT_A; no immediate motion"}
 ]
}
But Mode==TRUE from ANY to WAIT_A would reset auto every scan when Mode true, bad. Need only on entering auto from manual. Need ModePrev. Could say when Mode rising edge. But if we include edge flag. Maybe state "MANUAL" to handle mode. Let's design with explicit states MANUAL and AUTO states? But phase initial WAIT_A. Let's include "MANUAL" state. Transitions:
- Initial state? phase WAIT_A, but Mode unknown. If Mode false, go MANUAL. If Mode true, stay WAIT_A.
State machine states:
MANUAL: outputs manual mapping; CompletionLight off; phase forced WAIT_A. Transition to WAIT_A when Mode true (return to auto waits for A).
WAIT_A: auto idle. Transition to MANUAL when Mode false (clear auto state). Transition to MOVE_AB when Mode true && SensorA && ButtonA.
MOVE_AB: if Mode false -> MANUAL; if SensorB -> WAIT_B (stop same scan); else stay.
WAIT_B: if Mode false -> MANUAL; if SensorB && ButtonB -> MOVE_BC; else stay.
MOVE_BC: if Mode false -> MANUAL; if SensorC -> WAIT_C; else stay.
WAIT_C: if Mode false -> MANUAL; if SensorC && ButtonC -> DONE; else stay.
DONE: if Mode false -> MANUAL; if !SensorC -> WAIT_A (light off); else stay.
This includes MANUAL state. Initial phase WAIT_A per initial_conditions. But if initial Mode false, first scan transitions to MANUAL. The initial phase variable maybe WAIT_A. Good. P7 only auto states. Manual state phase maybe WAIT_A? To satisfy atomic wait_phase? In manual, phase not used. But if phase variable forced WAIT_A, then wait_phase true but P7 auto only, so fine. Completion light off. Good.

Need outputs in MANUAL: MotorForward = ForwardButton && !ReverseButton; MotorReverse = ReverseButton && !ForwardButton; CompletionLight false. In auto states: outputs per phase. MOVE_AB/BC: MotorForward true unless arrival same scan; MotorReverse false; CompletionLight false. WAIT_A/B/C: all off. DONE: MotorForward false, MotorReverse false, CompletionLight true (while SensorC). But if DONE and !SensorC same scan transition to WAIT_A, output light false in same scan. Good.

Need maybe handle arrival same scan in MOVE_AB to WAIT_B: output MotorForward false because stage 4 uses new phase? Scan order: stage 2 state transitions compute next phase; stage 4 unified output assignments based on next/current phase after transitions. Need specify outputs assigned from post-transition phase to ensure arrival stops same scan. Yes. In scan_execution_order stage 4: derive outputs from post-transition state (q[k+1]) so arrival/reset effects observed same scan. Good.

Need handle mode switch same scan: if Mode false, transition to MANUAL and outputs manual. But "Entering manual mode clears automatic state and completion; return to automatic waits for A." If Mode false, stage 2 sets phase=WAIT_A? But state MANUAL. In manual, phase forced WAIT_A. Completion off. Outputs manual. If Mode true next scan, state WAIT_A. Good.

Need edge sampling stage: sample Mode, buttons, sensors; compute rising edges of Mode? For manual-to-auto entry maybe state MANUAL + Mode true transitions to WAIT_A. No edge needed. But stage 1 can compute edges for buttons not used. Need mention "edge flags are computed for diagnostics; auto station buttons remain level-qualified". Could be okay. But required "stage 1 edge sampling" maybe they expect to sample rising edges. We'll include "Sample raw inputs; compute R_TRIG flags for ForwardButton, ReverseButton, ButtonA/B/C and ModePrev. Auto acceptance uses level-qualified SensorX & ButtonX per assumptions; edges are not used to create multiple transitions." This is explicit.

Need timer_plan. Since no timers required, use [] plus perhaps "No timers required; all transitions are level/phase-qualified; no PT durations or reset conditions." But key timer_plan maybe list. Could use:
"timer_plan": {
  "timers": [],
  "PT_durations": {},
  "reset_conditions": "None; no IEC timers are instantiated because the specification has no delay/debounce requirements."
}
This includes timers required, PT durations, reset conditions. Valid. But if expected list, maybe okay. The prompt says "timer_plan: timers required, PT durations, reset conditions". Object is fine. But "state_machine: list" and "formal_assertions: optional list". For timer_plan not explicitly list. Use object to provide all. Good.

Need priorities: safety and operational priorities list. Include:
1. Mode false/manual entry resets auto state, completion off, motor stops (or manual outputs? Actually mode false manual outputs may drive motor if buttons pressed. "Entering manual mode clears auto state and completion" not necessarily stop if forward button held. But safety priority: mode transition to manual must not continue automatic motion; manual requests can drive. So "manual transition clears auto phase; if manual buttons pressed, manual mapping applies." Safety interlock forward/reverse mutual exclusion. Opposing buttons produce neither direction. Arrival stop before processing. One transition per scan. Removal clears light. Auto no reverse. Button acceptance only in corresponding wait. Mode priority. Completion light only DONE with SensorC. Output interlock last.

Need initial_values:
{
 "phase": "WAIT_A",
 "state": "WAIT_A"? maybe "MANUAL"? initial_conditions phase WAIT_A. But with mode? Use "autoState": "WAIT_A", "manual"? Hmm. Use "phase": "WAIT_A", "MotorForward": false, "MotorReverse": false, "CompletionLight": false, "ModePrev": false, "ForwardButtonPrev": false, "ReverseButtonPrev": false, "ButtonAPrev": false, "ButtonBPrev": false, "ButtonCPrev": false
}
Maybe include "autoState": "WAIT_A" and "modeState": "MANUAL"? But initial_conditions only phase WAIT_A. If Mode false initially, scan 0 transitions to MANUAL. If Mode true, WAIT_A. To not invent, set "state": "WAIT_A" and "phase": "WAIT_A". But state machine includes MANUAL. Hmm. Could set "state": "WAIT_A" as initial; if Mode false, first scan enters MANUAL. But initial_conditions says phase WAIT_A. Good.

Need scan_execution_order explicit 4-stage. Provide array of 4 objects:
1. edge sampling: sample all inputs into I[k]; compute prev and rising edges for Mode/buttons; no output changes.
2. safety/reset priority & state transitions: apply Mode=false -> MANUAL/phase=WAIT_A/clear light; manual interlock and auto safety; evaluate at most one transition per scan in order: mode reset, arrival stop (MOVE_AB & SensorB -> WAIT_B; MOVE_BC & SensorC -> WAIT_C), station complete (WAIT_A & SensorA & ButtonA -> MOVE_AB; WAIT_B & SensorB & ButtonB -> MOVE_BC; WAIT_C & SensorC & ButtonC -> DONE), removal (DONE & !SensorC -> WAIT_A). Note arrival priority over complete? Need if in MOVE_AB and SensorB and ButtonB same scan? Arrival should stop to WAIT_B, not accept ButtonB? Assumption one transition per call. If arrival and button same scan in MOVE_AB, should transition to WAIT_B, not MOVE_BC. So priority: reset > safety/arrival > completion > removal? But removal in DONE. Need specify order. Also "Destination arrival stops movement before processing resumes" so arrival stop takes priority over any completion/start. In WAIT_B, if SensorB & ButtonB -> MOVE_BC. If in MOVE_AB and SensorB, go WAIT_B even if ButtonB true; one transition, no immediate MOVE_BC. Good. For WAIT_C & ButtonC, if SensorC true -> DONE. Removal in DONE if !SensorC. If DONE and SensorC false, go WAIT_A. If WAIT_C and !SensorC? stay. Good.
3. unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF: no timers; if any added, call unconditionally. For no timers, state "No timer FBs; placeholders for required timers only, never inside CASE/IF."
4. unified output assignments: compute MotorForward, MotorReverse, CompletionLight from post-transition state/phase with interlock. In manual: MF = ForwardButton && !ReverseButton; MR = ReverseButton && !ForwardButton; Light = false. In auto: MOVE_AB/BC and not arrival -> MF true; WAIT/DONE etc. But if post-transition state WAIT_B after arrival, MF false. DONE light true if SensorC. Also final interlock: if both MF and MR then both false; but auto never reverse. Completion light maybe only DONE & SensorC. Assign exactly once at end.

Need formal_assertions. Include maybe 6. Need use "G(...)". Ensure formulas over port names. Let's craft:
[
{"id":"A1","formula":"G(!(MotorForward && MotorReverse))"},
{"id":"A2","formula":"G((!Mode) -> ((MotorForward <-> (ForwardButton && !ReverseButton)) && (MotorReverse <-> (ReverseButton && !ForwardButton))))"},
{"id":"A3","formula":"G(Mode -> !MotorReverse)"},
{"id":"A4","formula":"G(CompletionLight -> SensorC)"},
{"id":"A5","formula":"G((Mode && SensorC && ButtonC) -> CompletionLight)"},
{"id":"A6","formula":"G((!SensorC) -> !CompletionLight)"}
]
A4 and A6 equivalent? A4 G(light -> SensorC). A6 G(!SensorC -> !light) same. Redundant. Could replace A6 with "G((Mode && SensorC) -> !MotorForward)"? Is that valid? At arrival at C, motor stops same scan. If in DONE, motor off. If in WAIT_C, off. If in manual, Mode false. If Mode true and SensorC true while MOVE_BC, post-transition WAIT_C and output off same scan. So valid. Add A6 "G((Mode && SensorC) -> !MotorForward)". But what if Mode true and SensorC true while MOVE_AB? Assumption one product and sensors not contradictory, so cannot. Good.
A5 "G((Mode && SensorC && ButtonC) -> CompletionLight)" valid? If in WAIT_C, transitions DONE and light true same scan. If in DONE, light true while SensorC. If in MOVE_BC and SensorC & ButtonC, arrival stop to WAIT_C, not DONE, light false. But assumption one product, if SensorC true in MOVE_BC, product arrives at C; ButtonC could be pressed same scan? Could operator press ButtonC before arrival? Maybe not. But formal assertion over ports could be violated if ButtonC true at arrival. To be safe, use "G((Mode && SensorC && ButtonC) -> CompletionLight)" might be too strong under simultaneous arrival and ButtonC. Better assert only "G(CompletionLight -> SensorC)" and "G((!SensorC) -> !CompletionLight)" redundant. Maybe include "G((Mode && SensorC) -> !MotorForward)" and "G((!Mode && ForwardButton && ReverseButton) -> (!MotorForward && !MotorReverse))". Good.

Need maybe include "G((Mode && SensorC) -> !MotorReverse)" but A3 covers auto no reverse. A4 completion implies sensor C. A5 light off when removed. Could use:
A1 interlock
A2 manual mapping
A3 auto no reverse
A4 completion implies product at C: G(CompletionLight -> SensorC)
A5 removal: G(!SensorC -> !CompletionLight) (redundant but clear)
A6 auto C arrival stop: G((Mode && SensorC) -> !MotorForward)
This is okay. A4 and A5 are logically equivalent, but one is safety invariant and one requirement. Redundancy okay but maybe not ideal. Could instead A5 "G((!Mode) -> !CompletionLight)" manual clears completion. That is valid? In manual mode, CompletionLight false. Yes. Good. Use A5 "G((!Mode) -> !CompletionLight)". Then A4 light -> SensorC. A6 auto C arrival stop. Good.

Need ensure A2 uses "<->" valid? It's a formula string; okay. JSON strings with quotes. Need escape? No.

Need final JSON only. Need no markdown. Need ensure valid JSON. Need include all keys. Let's construct.

Need word count <=2000. Our JSON likely ~1200 words. Fine.
